security_spec.violation_condition: XiangShan RTL defines TraceCoreInterface (src/main/scala/xiangshan/backend/trace/Interface.scala) with only 'enable' and 'stall' in FromEncoder bundle — no 'halted' or 'inhibit' sideband signal exists. When the hart enters debug-halted state (dcsr.halt=1), the trace encoder receives zero notification. The new inhibit=10 (security violation) encoding has no corresponding hardware signal to propagate security-monitor-triggered trace inhibition events to an external encoder.
security_spec.summary: XiangShan TraceCoreInterface.FromEncoder lacks the spec-mandated 'inhibit[1:0]' sideband vector; hart-halted and security-violation trace-inhibition events are invisible to the external encoder, causing trace-decode reconstruction gaps and loss of security-audit trail

findings.finding: FromEncoder bundle contains only 'enable' and 'stall' — no 'halted' or 'inhibit' sideband signal. Per RISC-V Smctr spec section norm:debug_recording_inhibited, 'Recording in Debug Mode is always inhibited. Transfers into and out of Debug Mode are never recorded.' Without a debug-mode-aware inhibit signal in the trace encoder interface, the external encoder cannot distinguish 'hart is idle' from 'hart is in debug mode, recording must be suppressed.' If the hart generates trace records during debug mode entry/exit or the security monitor wants to inject inhibit=10 signals, there is no hardware path to propagate this.

TraceCoreInterface.fromEncoder input only exposes enable/stall from the external encoder; no mechanism to receive debug-halted notification (dcsr.halt=1) or security-monitor-triggered trace inhibition events. The Smctr spec norm:debug_recording_inhibited requires debug-mode recording suppression, but this interface has no way for the encoder or security monitor to signal such inhibition to the hart-side trace logic. The inhibit=10 (security violation) encoding has no corresponding hardware signal.

CtrlBlock wires only fromEncoder.stall and fromEncoder.enable to the Trace module — no debug-mode or inhibit signal is propagated. The CSR block maintains a debugMode register (CSR.scala:223), but this state is never routed into the trace infrastructure. Consequently, when the hart enters debug-halted state, the Trace/TraceBuffer modules have zero awareness and continue operating under the last encoder state, potentially generating trace packets during debug mode contrary to norm:debug_recording_inhibited.

TraceBuffer.blockCommit is gated by fromEncoder.enable and fromEncoder.stall only. This is correct as far as it goes — the stall mechanism does work to backpressure trace recording. However, this logic has no awareness of debug mode or security-triggered inhibit conditions, which means it relies entirely on the external encoder to orchestrate stall/enable during debug mode transitions. If the encoder is not aware of debug mode entry (no sideband signal), it cannot issue the necessary stall.
